cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early negative reviews highlight complaints about locked gender options, account creation requirements, weak combat feedback, dated graphics, and an unfinished storyline.

claims.claim: The game features classes that are locked to specific genders.

citations.review_text: Gender-locked classes with no character customisation, Devs have no plans to ever add this :)

I've tried to get into this game twice and it's just not for me. My biggest points of contention: gender locked classes in 2026 (GGG is just as bad in this regard) and the graphics are just hideous. Like Grim Dawn arguably looks better/ has more style and that game is a decade old. 2nd time I've tried it since launch and I'm willing to give it a 3rd one day if things improve!

Gender locked classes... 
I didn't want to waste my time with this as a result... especially since both of the classes I was interested in playing were female. 
Refunded... maybe the game is good maybe it's bad, but I see no reason why a multiplayer game that released in 2024, should have gender lock on anything... they can use AI if they can't afford it, I couldn't care less as long as they deliver a better product.

CLASSES LOCKED TO GENDER. WHY?

I was excited to play this game, as it sounded really amazing, and in general, the reviews were good. But then I go to select my character, and not only can you not customize them [even though it clearly says that your character is customizable] but once again, classes are tied to gender. Why do I need to play as a man if I want to be a mage? I'm a woman, and I know it's shocking to the Last Epoch developers, but women enjoy gaming too! Classes should never be tied to gender. We should all get to play as the gender we want, and it shouldnt be locked behind it. Get with the times, and understand that women enjoy playing these types of games as well.

claims.claim: The storyline remains unfinished even after the full release.

citations.review_text: Unfinished story even after full release. No thank you
Gameplay is nice. Unfinished storyline though and "supporter pack" DLCs worth soem 70 EUR - thanks, get lost.

claims.claim: The game requires creating an external account with an email and display name instead of using a Steam username.

citations.review_text: Game requires an account (and email) instead of using your Steam user. If you want to change the name you chose it can only be done through a support ticket, so pick wisely....

Can't get past making an account name. I'm guessing I'll have to smash the keyboard and see if that works? Maybe do what Diablo does and allow the same names but append a number or create a randomly assigned one. So far, 10 of them have been taken, 3 are too long and the one I thought was going to work-the game crashed and now I cannot use it.

claims.claim: Combat animations and attacks lack weight or impactful feedback.

citations.review_text: The combat feels way too light and ragdoll effects are practically missing. Pretty disappointing for a modern ARPG where combat is supposed to be a central part of the gameplay.

I just wasn't having fun. My skill selections felt unimportant, animations/attacks didn't feel like they had weight, and the overall art just isn't up-to-snuff with competitors nowadays. If the game was significantly cheaper, I'm still unsure if I would be willing to purchase it.

claims.claim: The graphics and visual style are described as outdated, cheap, or hideous.

citations.review_text: I've tried to get into this game twice and it's just not for me. My biggest points of contention: gender locked classes in 2026 (GGG is just as bad in this regard) and the graphics are just hideous. Like Grim Dawn arguably looks better/ has more style and that game is a decade old. 2nd time I've tried it since launch and I'm willing to give it a 3rd one day if things improve!

Last Epoch feels like a lighter version of Path of Exile 1 rather than a truly different ARPG.
The graphics are also awful. The world, enemies, and effects do not give the game a strong identity, and a lot of it feels outdated or cheap.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players note connection issues and broken controller support alongside an offline mode option and complaints regarding broken promises on downloadable content.

claims.claim: Controller support is described as poorly implemented, with unresponsive buttons, lack of intuitive design, and restricted stick navigation.

citations.review_text: FORGET ABOUT playing on a controller.  Half the buttons don't work, it's not intuitive, and just not designed for that type of game play.  On a K/M, the click and drag of skills, sometimes works.  There's NO custom key binding.  The graphics at ultra settings on 5090 looks like they're from PS3 gen (or gives mobile game vibes). Another mid-ARPG, with so many bugs, not even its spells can kill them all.  And I get it, this might be a smaller studio.  But playing DOS I from Larian when they were still a small studio, is a much more premium experience - that it still holds up to this day.  This game is a pass.

Years later, after some patches that supposedly "improved controller support", the controller support is still terrible. Once in a while I keep coming back to try and get into the game again, but every time I'm stopped by this issue.

- The navigation in UI is limited to d-pad or by using right stick as the cursor. Can't use left stick for navigation.
- Can't use right stick for aiming while moving with the left stick during actual gameplay. All it does is make the cursor drift around the screen.

Awesome amazing time bought a pc just for this game! only complaint i have are the disconnects!

claims.claim: The game features an offline mode that allows playing without an active internet connection.

citations.review_text:
Bought this under the impression that this was a complete product yet its missing the last two chapters despite leaving early access. This NEEDS to be made clear on the product listing. 
Also it being on season 4 exacerbates this issue. why are we already on season 4 and the campaign isn't even done? I also hear of an upcoming expansion and from a quick google search, that leads me to believing that they are going to lock the last two chapters behind that expansion. 

As for the cosmetics that they apparently walked back their statement on, I don't really care. By the time you get to endgame in these ARPGs you'll hardly see your skin anyway, so if you don't like it just don't buy em, I personally don't think you'll be missing out on anything. I generally hate this practice anyway but it doesn't bother me as much in this genre. 

the good tho. It has an offline mode which is great for internet outages and steam deck, its also pretty well optimized and doesn't require a super computer. The build freedom feels really nice compared to the more streamlined build variety of Diablo.

Still, its a great ARPG and one of the better ones but they have been dropping the ball recently.

1. If you found Grim Dawn too old and unfriendly to new player
2, If you don't have powerful pc to run titan quest 2 (UE5 slop)
3. If you want a game that can play completely offline unlike Poe or diablo online nonsense 
4. If you want an ARPG that run reasonably well on steam deck

If you found yourself in similar situation like above, Last epoch is basically a few choice or the only choice that you have. Since, the ARPG genre is relative niche for whatever reason it is either too old or stupid choice made by executive like the always online for an offline game like Diablo 2 Resurrected.

claims.claim: The campaign lacks a completed story, leaving the final chapters missing.

citations.review_text:
Outside of the Krafton takeover this game has it's own issues. I feel like this game just tries to be POE lite, but it feels souless. I think they probably had a good idea originally to make an inbetween arpg between diablo and POE, but now that POE 2 has solved a lot of the complexity issues while maintaining content and Diablo has added some build diversity while adding content this game feels aimless. While they do have some build diveristy there isn't that much to the class or skill passive tree. You just pick up defense and your preferred damage type. I still think its a fun setup, but I wouldn't really consider it that more complex than Diablo. 
     The main problem I had with combat was that the skill lack impact, there isn't enough of sound/vfx/animation to make the skill feel impactful. The 2nd problem is there isn't enough difficulty. Through the whole campaign I never felt close to worrying about dying. Boss were barley above rares. Even into mapping there was no difficulty. It just felt boring. 
     The campaign story was not good or cohesive at all. I know story isn't the focus, but this one isn't interesting at all. Supposedly they were going to finish story after 1.0. I couldn't tell if it was done or not.
     I was also surprised how little content there was, for having 4 seasons there wasn't much there. I don't see how they can keep players with 2 seasons a year and so little content within the season. They probably would do better if it was annual expansions. Also I don't see how they are going to compete seasonally now that there is POE 1&2 and D4. It's a more crowded space and nothing I've seen sets this game apart. 
     Also the controller keybinds need updated for menu. There is a popular steam config that adds inventory, character, skill, and passives to long press of d pad. This works great and should be default. The current default of holding select while picking radial option with right stick then hoping you selection doesn't chang…

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-tier reviewers point to an incomplete campaign story, repetitive endgame progression, and weird gear scaling, though the offline mode remains a appreciated feature.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the main story campaign remains incomplete, leaving unresolved plot threads and ending on a cliffhanger.

citations.review_text: They did not even finish the campaign and it has been out of early access for two years now. Do not get this game. I finished the campaign and came back to hopefully finish the story to find out they have yet to even complete the campaign. This should still be in early access considering you never finish the game you just get to a point in the story then start doing "endgame" activities that are infinite and get no solid resolution

It's a fun game overall, with a unique take on skill evolution. You're able to greatly modify each ability - changing how the ability works, the elements, and more. There are a lot of synergies between abilities, and even items can alter how an ability works. The story is interesting and the end game content is an interesting twist.

The reason I give it a thumbs down is because after over 2 years of being released, the story remains unfinished. It ends on a very unsatisfying cliffhanger.

Game runs good, looks great, and provides a step in complexity in-between POE and Diablo, but that's where my positives end. 

- The game is insanely buggy, to the point where some skills straight up don't even work. 
- Controller support has not gotten like any updates in 3 years and menus are practically unusable with one. 
- The story sucks and is incomplete. 
- Only the main story characters are voiced and some other random things very early on. 
- Less actual build variety than it initially appears.
- Loot filters don't work correctly.
- Crafting is very restricted and SUPER rng.
- Respecing is atrocious.
- Game is incredibly grindy thanks to multiple layers of rng that can instantly brick your item.

I'm not going to write a long review like I normally do. The game is fun up until endgame where it becomes needlessly padded and grindy. I don't have an issue with things being grindy and padded if they are fun. But going 8-10 hours without getting any meaningful upgrades and leaving every single piece of gear on the ground sucks. Also, completing all the timelines only to be told you can't challenge the last boss without doing them ALL AGAIN with harder difficulties and with larger stability bars to fill is a big ol' punch in the ♥♥♥♥. I don't have time to waste on that ♥♥♥♥ when I can just watch the fight on YouTube and see how it ends then spend that time I would've been grinding doing literally anything else. 

EDIT: Also turns out there is literally NO narrative payout to doing the endgame. So unless you want to slowly grind away at boring ARPG content, avoid the endgame and stop after beating the story. Or don't play it at all. The main story leaves so many unresolved threads hanging for what they say are going to be resolved in the endgame that just aren't.

One of the most brutally mediocre games i've ever played. The perfect 5/10 on a true 10-point scale, average across the board. I've played all the classes and taken several of them into end-game across launch, Beneath Ancient Skies, and now Shattered Omens.

To get my pedigree out of the way, i love ARPGs. It's my absolute favorite genre and has been since Diablo 1 on the Playstation back in the late 90s. I've played almost every example of the genre that exists and have sunk a significant amount of time into all the current titans of the genre. All this to say that i know pretty well what how i feel about the genre and the goods and bads.

Almost nothing about Last Epoch stands out in any way. Aesthetically and stylistically it's generic medieval fantasy. Setting-wise the time travel stuff is nice on paper but ultimately they don't do anything interesting with it. Story-wise it's nothing you haven't seen before. Gameplay-wise it's about as generic ARPG as it gets, slightly more depth than Diablo 2 but less than Grim Dawn, Path of Exile, Titan Quest, etc. Like i could sit here and list point by point every single grievance i have with the game but ultimately the big things are this: The campaign is FAR too long for me to want to carry multiple characters per season into the endgame which isn't interesting either.

Itemization is borderline non-existent, nothing in the base game will exceed the items you get from seasonal stuff, a Rare item from a normal monster has 3-4 modifiers with like 20% to a few stats or melee damage and then Corrupted, Experimental, or Nemesis items come in with the steel chair with 5-8 modifiers that can reach into 100-200% boosts to stats, which also applies to Uniques, so you ignore literally everything that doesn't drop from those. Uniques themselves are also incredibly boring, they drop constantly and none of them are build-defining or really change how anything works. You'll still have the same handful of crazy modifier seasonal items f…

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the offline mode as a positive feature allowing gameplay without server crashes or connection issues.

citations.review_text: If you've played all the other ARPGs already and you need an itch scratcher, you've been sleeping on this one too long. Must play for ARPG fans. Every made-up random build I've tried feels really fun to use and the forge system makes creating gear upgrades in a pinch when you really need a boost. I could rant about how nice it runs on the Steam Deck but its a relatively small game for this genre and its worth the try if you want a portable ARPG to play or something to switch between PC(I play entirely on Offline Mode lately). Genuinely surprised at where this game ended up on my favorite ARPG list.

Fun ARPG alternative to PoE and Diablo 4 that is better at some things but worst at others. The crafting in this game is hands down the best version in any ARPG I've ever played! Also gets a +1 for having an offline mode.

After hundreds of hours poured into Path of Exile and Diablo, I can honestly say that Last Epoch has completely won me over and taken the top spot for me. It hits that perfect sweet spot that the other two seem to have lost along the way.
The leveling is incredibly smooth and actually fun, while the itemization and crafting system are by far the best designed out of anything I've ever played—you feel real progression instead of just being at the mercy of absurd RNG.
Another huge plus is that you can play completely offline, without the headache of server crashes or lag. On top of that, I absolutely love that you aren't forced into leagues to enjoy the game. You can just chill in Legacy and still have access to all the content, without that constant pressure to start from scratch every few months if you don't have the time. For me, it respects the player's time so much better and is exactly what an ARPG should be.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players cite constant disconnects, performance drops, broken passive nodes, and unappealing default gear visuals alongside complaints about the campaign.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the main story campaign is unfinished and incomplete.

citations.review_text: It's an alright ARPG, but I honestly can't recommend this game. Performance issues, jank, unfinished story, slow updates, missing features and tooltips, even the monetization model is unbearable and makes your characters visually unappealable. I wouldn't mind buying another expansion for this game if it would both polish and improve the base game enough, but I still feel somewhat duped when I look at this game in its current state. End of the day feels more financially motivated, rather than providing you with a fun experience, and at this point, I'm not even sure if this game will come back from this slump.
Really looking forward to the free Orobyss expansion. I enjoyed playing through the main story, but the ending does feel incomplete as of now.

This is a great base of a game.

But it's still not a great game yet.

As other reviewers have pointed out, the main story is not finished, but we're getting seasons with new features and peacemeal dribbles of the main campaign.  To be fair, the story isn't... A+ material, but it feels representative of how the devs approach this game.

So if the main story isn't complete, how is the "post-game"?  I'll describe it with comparing to Path of Exile's endgame:

Path of Exile: A casserole with 20 different ingredients that somehow shockingly meld together.  And even if you don't like one ingredient, you can use the chef's tools to take that ingredient out and replace it with more of the others!

Last Epoch: A casserole that's all noodles, ham, and cheese.  You can add salt or pepper, maybe add a little more ham or cheese, but that's about it.  It's good at first, but underseasoned and there's only more ham casserole all the way through.

This is understandable, PoE has been cooking a loooot longer.  And Last Epoch has some great things!  The crafting is excellent! (Mostly.)  The skill trees are a great balance between complexity and creativity! (When they're balanced right.)  It's really pretty! (Which I'm pretty sure why it takes so long to get minor updates to this game.)

But you can't have both a not finished story and a meh endgame.  PoE has an alright story but excellent endgame.  Grim Dawn has a a meh endgame but a great campaign.  Diablo 4... exists.

So... I guess in the end, I'm still hoping that they finally nail one or the other here.  You can see I've played this plenty.  There are some great bones, and it's a good game for playing while listening to streams or such.

But in the end, I guess I would direct you elsewhere until one of the devs actually finish cooking.

The game was great at first, but then it got bought by Krafton, and since then it has barely evolved. 

The story is still unfinished, and it honestly feels like the game has been left to rot. 

The devs seem to be doing the bare minimum just to keep it on life support.

Devs lost the plot.  The game has done nothing but change for the worse. Tons of long standing bugs, single player story never finished, but the cash shop works alright. There are better ARPGs out there.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that some new passive nodes and items released in updates fail to function or work inconsistently.

citations.review_text: Absolutely unplayable vibe coded slop for over a year. In the last year almost every single new passive node and item added to the game has either flat out not worked or has only sometimes worked. 0/10 would not recommend in the current condition.

They're implementing a visionary approach to customer service by polling on their official forums on what to prioritize fixing in their own bug-riddled game. These include item stats not applying or calculating correctly, unique items not working correctly, affix behavior issues, and item loss/duplication. Some of these bugs have existed for a long time, since early access, and have never been addressed. Truly a masterful display in game management and QA/QC.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign as a strict and repetitive linear slog.

citations.review_text: One of my favourite ARPGs, yet I'm giving it thumbs down. My biggest issue with the game is the campaign and its strict linearity, which for me had become a slog. I have zero appetite for trying out new stuff in the new season because I'll have to do the same things for ten hours that I've done numerous times already. Please transform the levelling process into an adventure mode-like style, as it is in D3.

Was pretty good up to some point, now it's KRAFTON.
Campaign is a chore, still no new characters. Replayability on the long run sucks.

First ARPG for me, so bear that in mind. Gameplay is okay, can pick between WASD and mouse clicks - I ended up staying with mouse clicks like RTS games do. Graphics look good enough (but I never cared about those realistic style graphics so....). I had to import loot filters for a long while but tweaking those eventually became easier. I have been told crafting is much more forgiving than PoE2 but I don't play that so take with 10 buckets of salt. Story is intriguing, seeing the map differences between eras fascinate me.

 My gripes so far (in Season 4): Player Character doesn't have a dedicated text channel output. I'm a little hard of hearing at this point, so it's a bummer that I don't know what my character is commenting. We cannot customize the chat channels for that matter... I'd like the ability to have a separate (or combined) chat channel with NPC and PC chatters.
Omen windows eat my frames like no tomorrow. So many entitites, the omen legit dies within 1 gulp of water while clearing the adds take upwards of minutes.
Difficulty getting certain items due to poor drop rate and/or inability to target? farm (skill issue and desire detector I guess?). I'm looking at you, Aaron's Will -_ -

The game has so much potential yet every time I've tried to come back its constantly plagued by random disconnects and super long loading when going to new areas. along with the issues with coop and lack of regular trading.

I had a read of some of the reviews for this game and thought I'd drop my two cents.
Seems a lot of people are just focused on the direction the parent company is going in the future vs. the state of the game.
For me personally:
I think the gameplay is very enjoyable, I enjoy the customization on a number of different levels and the interactions that the unique items and forging brings to the game.
Visually, I think the game looks great! I think that the engine is not the best and there is some occasionally choppy gameplay, but for me doesn't detract from the beauty of the world, and how impressive and impactful I find most of the skills and abilities.
The systems in the game take a long time to uncover fully and sometimes they are not very well explained, but I think for me this only added to the depth of the gameplay after a few hundred hours there was still more for me to learn/discover.
I invested hundreds of hours into grinding Diablo 3, and I would say that this is maybe the closest representation I've found to that gameplay (far moreso than the current state of DIV) and is something that I can pick up and play for an hour at a time and enjoy it or playing for an entire day.
The offline mode this game has, puts it in a tier above for me for playing on handheld and travelling - bad on steamdeck (more based on the engine than the specs) great on Legion Go 2 Z2 Extreme
Last Epoch for me scratches a lot of itches and I believe the game is a great balanced middle ground between the smoothness of DIV and the complexity of POE/2

I'll caveat this whole review by saying that I will be disappointed to see this game head down a path focused on profits over serving the community (where I think most of the devs would probably align) but right now I think the game is fantastic.

citations.review_text: It's an alright ARPG, but I honestly can't recommend this game. Performance issues, jank, unfinished story, slow updates, missing features and tooltips, even the monetization model is unbearable and makes your characters visually unappealable. I wouldn't mind buying another expansion for this game if it would both polish and improve the base game enough, but I still feel somewhat duped when I look at this game in its current state. End of the day feels more financially motivated, rather than providing you with a fun experience, and at this point, I'm not even sure if this game will come back from this slump.

This games gameplay and leveling systemas are fun but I miss how ARPGs used to be, looking sick looking loot while you grinding to get that one drop. Now you pay for cosmetics and dealing with multiple levels of RNG to get the build you want. My Character looks so ugly in the end game that it makes you want to buy Cosmetics but I just cant. Grew up when gaming used to be different and I cant climatize to how games are developed and moenitized nowdays.
